reason: I studied late and wish someone had asked what the early years were for. Let the school say, in the open.
Families should have the majority, but a national floor stops some schools doing nothing at all.
Teachers get told what to do anyway. A funded rule with checks at least means somebody turns up.
Heads and teachers know their pupils. Make them publish what they do and why, then let parents judge.
Keep the rule. In my day the exam board set it and it held. Add the money so nobody loses subjects.
My lad's school rushed him into exams at twelve. Let the people in the building decide, in public.
Councils and panels are more committees. Parents should pick a school and leave when it lets them down.
A family majority sounds right, with a floor so reading and maths stay. I don't trust a panel with nothing underneath.
Local people know what their school needs. Publish the plan and the results so we can see if it works.
I want a say, but not if it ends in a talking shop. Have a floor, and elected, so I know who to ask.
Standards matter most. Let parents choose and vote with their feet; the rest is more paperwork.
Let the school decide in the open. If exams rule the early years, say so and explain why.
